summary:
Mission AURORA is an interactive 3D Mars survival simulation designed to make space science engaging and accessible for young explorers. It allows users to experience the challenges of operating a Martian habitat by exploring its environment, managing essential life-support systems, and making real-time decisions that directly affect crew survival.
The project addresses the challenge of making complex space science concepts easier to understand through interactive, experience-based learning rather than traditional textbook-focused education. It simulates five interconnected habitat systems: solar power generation and battery storage, air and water life support, hydroponic food production, radiation-protected shelter, and communication with Earth. Through simulated solar weather events, energy limitations, and operational decisions, users learn how these systems depend on one another to keep a Mars crew safe.
Mission AURORA is important because it transforms abstract scientific concepts into practical learning experiences. By combining interactive exploration, scientific simulations, and decision-making challenges, it encourages curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving while introducing the next generation to the realities of human space exploration. Its ultimate vision is to inspire young learners to explore Mars, understand space science, and develop the skills needed for future exploration missions
details:
Project Details

Mission AURORA is an interactive 3D Mars survival simulation developed to introduce users to the scientific and technological challenges of human exploration on Mars. The project allows users to explore a simulated Martian habitat, interact with essential life-support systems, and make decisions that influence the survival of the crew.

The simulation focuses on five interconnected systems: solar power generation and battery storage, air and water life support, hydroponic food production, radiation-protected shelter, and communication with Earth. Users experience simulated solar weather events, energy limitations, and operational challenges while learning how each system contributes to a sustainable Mars habitat.

The main benefit of Mission AURORA is its educational approach. Instead of learning space science only through textbooks, users can explore scientific concepts through interactive experiences and decision-making. It aims to improve curiosity, critical thinking, scientific understanding, and problem-solving skills among young learners.

The project was developed using React and TypeScript, with TSX for application components and JSON for structured data. Google AI Studio was also used as an AI-assisted development tool.

What makes Mission AURORA creative is its combination of space exploration, interactive simulation, and survival-based learning. It connects multiple habitat systems into one learning experience, helping users understand how energy, life support, food production, radiation protection, and communication depend on one another.

During development, the team considered educational accessibility, scientific relevance, system interdependence, user interaction, and the challenges of maintaining human survival in the Martian environment.

Our ultimate goal is to inspire the next generation of explorers, make space science more accessible, and encourage interest in future human missions to Mars.
